messages:
lex_support: FYI support ticket from BrightPay — customers reporting repeated streaming 504s during long completions (several requests >30s). They reported client-side reconnects and lost partial streams. Request id: req_2026-03-17-xy1234 :frowning:

lex_support: sample logs attached from customer (pasted). They see gateway 504s then immediate 502s, intermittent 200s after retry. Impacting checkout flows.

sai_oncall: thanks Lex. Can you drop the request ids + region? also which model + route they were hitting?

lex_support: region eu-west-1, model: gptx-stream-v2, route: /v1/respond/stream, req ids: req_2026-03-17-xy1234, req_2026-03-17-xy1288

morgan_sre: looking at infra metrics now. Observed connection pool saturation on edge-proxy euw-03 around 1755554000-1755554500. p50 latency normal, p99 spiked to ~18s, SYN backlog increased. No large deploys in window.

aj_dev: checked runtime logs for gptx-stream-v2 shards — a few pods reported long GC pauses and repeated KV cache eviction. See snippet: ```[2026-03-17T10:20:15Z] shard-7 WARN kvcache: eviction_count=432, ttl_miss=21
[2026-03-17T10:20:19Z] runtime INFO inference: request=req_2026-03-17-xy1234 total_token_time=14520ms backend_wait=12000ms```

kim_eng: that backend_wait ~12s suggests blocking in kernel selection path or remote cache calls. Could be a hot prefix causing oversized batching + stall. Any large batch traces?

morgan_sre: yes, batch sizes spiked to 256 for a short window. Autoscaler didn't spin up fast enough due to allocation lag.

sai_oncall: mitigation proposal: 1) enable route-level streaming timeout extension to 45s for affected route (short-term), 2) force-fallback to light model redwood-llm-small for BrightPay (config flag), 3) reduce max batch size to 64 on the runtime for this model, 4) trigger canary with updated batching config. Thoughts?

aj_dev: +1. Also add a quick KV-cache warmup / prewarming for hot prefixes and enable conservative batch-splitting to avoid head-of-line stalls.

kim_eng: we should also rollback the recent kernel optimizer patch we rolled out to shard-7 if that correlates. Can you confirm patch versions?

morgan_sre: patch v2.14.7 deployed to euw-03 at 1755553900 — correlates with first spike. I'm going to pin that node group out of rotation and start draining shard-7 for a hotfix.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout initiated: config=batching-limits-64, timeout-extend-45s targeting euw-03, rollout_id=canary-1755554321-1

lex_support: informing BrightPay about temporary fallback to redwood-llm-small and extended timeout. Asking for any additional examples. :thumbsup:

sai_oncall: immediate action items:
- morgan_sre: drain and isolate euw-03 scaled node group (owner)
- aj_dev: prepare hotfix to batch-splitting + KV warmup (owner)
- kim_eng: verify kernel optimizer revision and prepare rollback plan (owner)
- lex_support: coordinate customer comms and confirm degraded fallback OK (owner)

kam_eng (typo in earlier message corrected): sorry new name — ignore

aj_dev: I pushed a hotfix branch with conservative batching and KV prewarm hooks, deploying to canary now. Command: ```kubectl apply -f canary-batching-175555.yaml```

morgan_sre: draining euw-03 nodes now. ETA ~7m to fully drain. I will monitor connection backlog.

incident-bot: War room created: #warroom-1755554321-streaming-504s. Playbook: streaming-504s-mitigation-v3 invoked.

lex_support: BrightPay confirms they can accept fallback for next 2 hours while we investigate. They asked for postmortem and ETA on restoration.

sai_oncall: temporary customer-facing statement: "We're investigating intermittent streaming timeouts impacting some EU customers. We're routing affected traffic to a fallback model and tuning batching; we'll follow up with a postmortem." I'll send official comms after we confirm mitigation stabilizes.

aj_dev: canary metrics look good: p99 latency reduced from 18s -> 6s on canary. No 504s in the last 3 minutes for canary traffic.

morgan_sre: euw-03 drain complete. Old nodes pinned out. Rolling out fix to rest of euw cluster in a staged window.

kim_eng: looked at kernel optimizer diff — edge-case in kernel selection for long sequences that can block when batch split heuristics are mispredicted. I'll roll back v2.14.7 on euw-03 and open PR for safer heuristics.

aj_dev: patch rolled to euw-eu1, euw-03 canary stable. Monitoring.

lex_support: Customer happy for now. They asked for root cause + action items. Let's capture in postmortem.

sai_oncall: Post-incident action items (collect & owners):
- RC1: Roll back v2.14.7 optimizer on eu clusters + add test for long-seq heuristic (kim_eng)
- RC2: Implement conservative batch-splitting and KV prewarm by default for streaming routes (aj_dev)
- RC3: Improve autoscaler reaction to hot prefix bursts (morgan_sre)
- RC4: Add route-level circuit-breaker + fallback routing for premium customers (product/eng) (sai_oncall)
__meta_note: This JSON represents a single Slack thread as a continuous string. Field names match agents.md requirements; no title included.
